entry: Biblical patriarch and figure in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. He is claimed to have lived 969 years, the longest lifespan in the [[Bible]]. In the [[Book of Genesis]] he is the son of Enoch, father of Lamech, and grandfather of [[Noah]]. He is also named in 1 Chronicles and the Gospel of Luke. Commentators have offered explanations for his age, including myth, mistranslation, and the impression that part of Genesis takes place in a very distant past. His name has become synonymous with longevity.

Simplest primary [[Amine|amine]], an organic compound with the formula CH₃NH₂. It is a colorless gas and a derivative of [[Ammonia|ammonia]] in which one hydrogen atom is replaced by a methyl group. It is sold dissolved in [[Methanol|methanol]], [[Ethanol|ethanol]], tetrahydrofuran, or [[Water|water]], or as the anhydrous gas in pressurized metal containers. It has a strong odor similar to rotten fish and is used as a building block for many commercially available compounds. Industrially, it is made by reacting ammonia with methanol in the presence of an aluminosilicate catalyst. It was first prepared in 1849 by Charles-Adolphe Wurtz.

Chloride [[Salt (chemistry)|salt]] used as a [[Dye|dye]] and as a medication. It is mainly used to treat methemoglobinemia, converting methemoglobin back to [[Hemoglobin|hemoglobin]], and has also been used to treat [[Malaria|malaria]] for more than a century. It was first prepared in 1876 by Heinrich Caro and is on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines. It is typically given by injection into a vein, and common side effects include headache, nausea, and vomiting. Outside its established medical use, its safety and effectiveness are unproven, and it is potentially toxic.

Central nervous system stimulant sold as Ritalin and Concerta. It is used to treat [[Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder|ADHD]] and [[Narcolepsy|narcolepsy]] and is believed to block the reuptake of [[Dopamine|dopamine]] and norepinephrine. Its effectiveness for ADHD is modestly lower than that of [[Amphetamine|amphetamine]], but it is preferred as a first-line treatment in children. Common side effects include loss of appetite, [[Weight loss|weight loss]], and trouble sleeping. Dependence and withdrawal are mainly reported with high-dose or non-medical use. In 2023 it was the 50th most commonly prescribed medication in the United States, with more than 13 million prescriptions.

Figure of speech in which a concept is referred to by the name of something associated with it. For example, "suit" may refer to a business executive, banker, or lawyer, and "the [[White House]]" can denote the U.S. presidential administration. Unlike metaphor, which relies on analogy, metonymy rests on general association between the two things. It is common in everyday speech and appears in some [[Poetry|poetry]] and much [[Rhetoric|rhetoric]]. Synecdoche and metalepsis are considered specific types of metonymy.

Base unit of length in the [[International System of Units]] (SI); symbol m. Since 2019 it has been defined as the distance traveled by [[Light|light]] in a vacuum during 1/299,792,458 of a second, with the second fixed by the hyperfine transition frequency of cesium. The meter was first defined in 1791 by the French National Assembly as one ten-millionth of the distance from the [[Equator]] to the [[North Pole]] along a great circle through Paris, setting 10,000 km as a quarter of Earth's polar circumference. In 1799 it was tied to a prototype bar, and in 1960 to a number of wavelengths of a krypton-86 emission line. The current definition was adopted in 1983 and modified slightly in 2002. Long distances are usually given in km, [[Astronomical unit|astronomical units]], or [[Light-year|light-years]] rather than in larger metric multiples.

Mathematical [[Set (mathematics)|set]] with a notion of [[Distance|distance]] between its points. The distance is given by a function called a metric, which gives zero distance from a point to itself, positive distance between distinct points, symmetry, and the triangle inequality. Metric spaces provide a general setting for studying concepts of [[Mathematical analysis|mathematical analysis]] and [[Geometry|geometry]], such as balls and completeness. The most familiar example is three-dimensional [[Euclidean space]], and a [[Sphere|sphere]] with angular distance is another. Metrics can also express nonphysical distance: the Hamming distance between 100-character Unicode strings counts the characters that must change. Riemannian manifolds, normed [[Vector space|vector spaces]], and graphs can all be viewed as metric spaces, and the p-adic numbers are the completion of the rational numbers under a certain metric.

System of measurement built on standard base units and [[Decimal|decimal]] prefixes such as kilo and milli. The [[International System of Units]] (SI) is the main example, and other metric systems include the centimetre–gram–second system and the gravitational metric system. The SI has seven base units: the [[Metre|meter]], [[Kilogram|kilogram]], [[Second|second]], ampere, kelvin, mole, and candela. Derived units include the hertz and the [[Newton (unit)|newton]], and degrees [[Celsius]] are a shifted scale. Today all base units are defined by physical constants rather than physical prototypes. The SI is the official system of weights and measures in almost all countries, but the United States has resisted full adoption and continues to use other systems. Adopting the metric system is called metrication.

American film and television production and distribution company, headquartered in Culver City, California. Founded on April 17, 1924, by Marcus Loew, it combined Metro Pictures, Goldwyn Pictures, and [[Louis B. Mayer]] Pictures and became known for its musicals and many [[Academy Awards]]. Its franchises include [[James Bond]], [[Rocky]], and [[The Pink Panther]]. After changes of ownership, including [[Ted Turner]]'s 1986 purchase of MGM/UA, the company filed for bankruptcy in 2010. [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] agreed in 2021 to buy it for $8.45 billion, and the deal closed in 2022.

Capital region and largest [[Metropolitan area|metropolitan area]] of the [[Philippines]], formally the National Capital Region (NCR). It covers 636 sq km and had 14,001,751 residents in 2024. It includes sixteen highly urbanized cities, among them [[Manila]] and [[Quezon City]], plus the municipality of Pateros. The region accounts for 36% of the Philippines' gross domestic product and hosts the embassies of other countries. It hosted the 1987, 2017, and 2026 ASEAN summits. Its low-lying geography leaves it exposed to [[Typhoon|typhoons]] and [[Flood|flooding]].

Science-fiction action-adventure video game franchise created by [[Nintendo]]. It follows the bounty hunter Samus Aran. The first game was released on the [[Nintendo Entertainment System]] in 1986. *Super Metroid* (1994) for the [[Super Nintendo Entertainment System|Super Nintendo]] expanded the formula, and the first 3D entry, *Metroid Prime*, appeared on the [[GameCube]] in 2002. The series blends the platforming of [[Super Mario Bros.]] with the exploration of [[The Legend of Zelda]]. Its early games helped define the Metroidvania subgenre. The series had sold more than 17.44 million copies as of 2012.

Science of [[Measurement|measurement]] and its application. It establishes common units and is divided into three overlapping activities: defining units, realizing them in practice, and traceability, which links practical measurements to reference standards. Its sub-fields are scientific or fundamental metrology, which establishes units; applied or industrial metrology, which applies measurement to manufacturing and other processes; and legal metrology, which regulates measuring instruments and methods. Modern metrology grew out of the [[French Revolution]], when a length standard based on a natural source was proposed, leading to the decimal-based [[Metric system|metric system]] in 1795. The first permanent standard on record is the royal Egyptian [[Cubit|cubit]], carved from black [[Granite|granite]] in 2900 BC. The [[International System of Units]] (SI) evolved from the metric system after a 1960 resolution at the 11th General Conference on Weights and Measures.

German expressionist science-fiction [[Silent film|silent film]] directed by [[Fritz Lang]]. Written by Lang and Thea von Harbou from her 1925 novel, it stars Brigitte Helm, Gustav Fröhlich, Alfred Abel, and Rudolf Klein-Rogge. Its story follows the son of the city master as he tries to bridge the gulf between the classes. Critics praised its visuals and special effects but accused the story of being naïve; [[H. G. Wells]] called it "silly". The film was cut substantially after its German premiere, and a 2010 restoration came within five minutes of Lang's original running time. It was inscribed on [[UNESCO]]'s Memory of the World register in 2001, and it ranked 67th in *Sight and Sound*'s 2022 critics' poll.

Encyclopedic [[Art|art]] museum in [[New York City]], colloquially known as the Met. Founded in 1870, it is the largest art museum in the Americas and, by floor area, the fourth-largest museum in the world. The main building on Fifth Avenue, along the Museum Mile at the eastern edge of [[Central Park]], covers about 2 million square feet, its first portion built in 1880. The permanent collection of 1.5 million works is divided into 17 curatorial departments and ranges from [[Egypt|ancient Egypt]] and [[Classical antiquity|classical antiquity]] to European Old Masters and modern American art. Its holdings also include [[Islamic art]], Asian and African art, musical instruments, costumes, and [[Weapon|weapons]] and armor. With 5,727,258 visitors in fiscal year 2025, it was the most-visited museum in the United States.

Densely populated urban agglomeration and the surrounding territory that shares its industries, commercial areas, transport network, and housing. A metropolitan area includes contiguous built-up areas bound to the center by employment or other commerce, which may extend into other political entities. East Hampton, New York, on [[Long Island]], is considered part of the New York metropolitan area. In 2020 several international bodies, including the [[OECD]] and the World Bank, agreed on a framework that defines a "functional urban area" as a city and its commuting zone, where at least 15% of employed residents work in the city. In the [[United States]], metropolitan statistical areas are built around an urbanized core of at least 50,000 people. Population figures for one metro area can vary by millions.

1846–1848 invasion of Mexico by the United States. The war followed the 1845 American annexation of [[Texas]], which Mexico still considered its territory. The boundary dispute centered on the [[Rio Grande]], which the United States and Texas claimed, while Mexico claimed the more northerly Nueces River. President [[James K. Polk]] offered $25 million for the disputed territory and California, but Mexico refused. After Mexican forces repelled U.S. troops on April 25, 1846, Polk persuaded Congress to declare war. U.S. forces captured [[Mexico City]] in September 1847. The 1848 Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ended the war: Mexico gave up present-day California, Nevada, and Utah and parts of Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Wyoming, and relinquished its claims to Texas. The U.S. agreed to pay $15 million for war damages. The new acquisitions intensified the debate over [[Slavery in the United States|slavery]], and some scholars see the war as leading to the [[American Civil War]].

Nationwide armed struggle in [[Mexico]], 1910–1920. Primarily a [[Civil war|civil war]], the Revolution drew in foreign powers with economic interests in Mexico, particularly the United States. It led to the deaths of around one million people, mostly noncombatants. The conflict began when Francisco I. Madero challenged [[Porfirio Díaz]] in the 1910 presidential election, was jailed, and called for an armed uprising. Díaz resigned in May 1911. [[Emiliano Zapata]] rebelled in Morelos, demanding agrarian reform. In February 1913 generals staged a coup, and Madero was forced to resign and then assassinated on the orders of Victoriano Huerta. By 1915 the Constitutionalist faction under Venustiano Carranza had defeated [[Pancho Villa]]. The Constitution of 1917 established universal male suffrage, workers' rights, land reform, and [[Secularism|secularism]]. From 1920 to 1940 revolutionary generals held the presidency, and the party they founded in 1929 ruled Mexico until the 2000 presidential election.

Armed conflict, 1810–1821, that ended Spanish rule of [[New Spain]]. It began with the Cry of Dolores on September 16, 1810, when priest [[Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla]] rallied an initially disorganized revolt. Hidalgo was captured and executed in 1811, and José María Morelos led a second phase until his execution in 1815. The insurgency then became guerrilla warfare under Vicente Guerrero, and a military stalemate lasted until 1821. [[Napoleon]]'s 1808 invasion of Spain had undermined royal legitimacy, and in 1820 Spanish liberals overthrew Ferdinand VII, prompting Mexican conservatives to seek independence. Former royalist Agustín de Iturbide allied with Guerrero under the Plan of Iguala. The combined army entered [[Mexico City]] in September 1821, and the viceroy Juan O'Donojú signed the Treaty of Córdoba. The ephemeral First Mexican Empire was overthrown, and a federal republic was declared in 1823.

Culinary traditions of [[Mexico]], rooted in Mesoamerican food practices. Its ingredients and methods arise from early farming communities such as the Olmec and Maya, who domesticated [[Maize|maize]] and developed nixtamalization, the process of treating corn with lime. Successive groups, including the [[Teotihuacan|Teotihuacanos]], added their own cooking methods. The Mexica later formed the multi-ethnic Triple Alliance, the [[Aztec Empire]], and its foodways became infused into the cuisine. Native staples include corn, turkey, beans, squash, avocados, tomatoes, cacao, vanilla, agave, and chili peppers. After the Spanish conquest, Spaniards introduced beef, pork, chicken, cheese, rice, sugar, and olive oil. African influence came through [[Slavery|slavery]] in New Spain. Traditional Mexican cuisine was inscribed in 2010 on the [[UNESCO]] Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Ongoing asymmetric armed conflict between the Mexican government and drug trafficking syndicates. President Felipe Calderón launched Operation Michoacán in 2006, deploying tens of thousands of troops against cartels in [[Ciudad Juárez]], [[Tijuana]], and elsewhere. Arrests and killings of leaders splintered the cartels into smaller, more violent factions. Estimates put the death toll above 120,000 by 2013, not counting 27,000 missing. Successive governments have kept militarized tactics, which have drawn criticism for extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and [[Torture|torture]]. Law enforcement has also been criticized for corruption and collusion with cartels.

American [[Organized crime|organized crime]] figure associated with [[Gambling|gambling]] and illicit finance. Lansky emerged from New York City's Jewish underworld. He was a close friend of Charles "Lucky" Luciano, and historians describe him as a financial organizer who helped build cooperation between Jewish and Italian-American criminals, including the National Crime Syndicate. Lansky's casino interests in [[Havana]] were lost after [[Fidel Castro]] took power. Despite nearly fifty years of investigation by the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]], he was convicted only of illegal gambling offenses. Historians consider claims of extraordinary wealth unproven.

American actress and activist. She first gained notice as Allison MacKenzie in the [[Soap opera|soap opera]] *Peyton Place*, and achieved international acclaim as Rosemary in [[Roman Polanski]]'s *Rosemary's Baby* (1968). She was briefly married to [[Frank Sinatra]] and appeared in thirteen of [[Woody Allen]]'s films beginning in 1982. In 1992 she publicly accused Allen of sexually abusing their adopted daughter; he was not charged and has denied the allegation. She is a [[UNICEF]] Goodwill Ambassador, and [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named her one of the most influential people in the world in 2008.

Coastal city (pop., 2020: 442,241) in southeastern [[Florida]], the county seat of Miami-Dade County. Its metropolitan area, with an estimated 6.39 million residents, is the largest urban economy in Florida, with a 2023 [[Gross domestic product|gross domestic product]] of $533.674 billion. Miami is a leader in finance, commerce, and international trade, and its downtown has one of the largest concentrations of international banks in the United States. About 70.2 percent of the city's population identifies as Hispanic or Latino (2020), and Miami has been called the "Gateway to Latin America." PortMiami is the busiest cruise port in the world in passenger traffic. The metropolitan area is the second-most visited in the United States after [[New York City]], with more than four million visitors in 2022. The city was founded on land owned by Julia Tuttle, a citrus grower, and is noted as the only major U.S. city founded by a woman.

American crime drama television series that ran on [[NBC]] from 1984 to 1989. Executive-produced by [[Michael Mann]], it stars [[Don Johnson]] as James "Sonny" Crockett and Philip Michael Thomas as Ricardo "Rico" Tubbs, undercover detectives in [[Miami]]. Unlike traditional police procedurals, it drew on 1980s culture, including rock and pop music, [[Fashion|fashion]], and sports cars such as the [[Ferrari]] Testarossa. It prioritized music and stylized visuals over elaborate writing. The series heavily inspired the 2002 video game *Grand Theft Auto: Vice City*, and Mann directed a 2006 film adaptation.

Group of 37 phyllosilicate [[Mineral|minerals]] whose crystals split easily into fragile, elastic plates along perfect basal cleavage. Mica has a layered structure in which two silica sheets bond to an octahedral sheet, with interlayer [[Potassium|potassium]], [[Sodium|sodium]], or [[Calcium|calcium]] ions. It is common in [[Granite|granite]], pegmatite, and [[Schist|schist]], and occasionally found as flakes in [[Sedimentary rock|sedimentary rock]]. The most economically important members are muscovite, a potassium-aluminum silicate, and phlogopite, a potassium-magnesium silicate. Mica's high dielectric strength and heat resistance make it useful as an electrical insulator in capacitors, and it is also used in paints, drywall, and cosmetics. Muscovite withstands temperatures up to about 700°C.
